topic: The space station is only about 250 miles up, yet reaching it takes hours: why Crew-13's 7 h 55 min trip was the fastest by a US spacecraft

through_line.name: the little white crew capsule
through_line.progression: the capsule rides the rocket up, falls short going straight up, then chases the station around the planet, each chase shorter than the last
through_line.resolution: the capsule clicks onto the station and the loop returns to it closing in from below

blocks.vo_line: The space station is closer than you think. Roughly two hundred fifty miles overhead, yet astronauts can spend a full day reaching it.
blocks.through_line_state: the capsule closes in on the station from below
shots: MEDIUM, slow push-in: the little capsule races up from below toward the big station, thrusters puffing
EXTREME CLOSE-UP, static: the capsule's nose cone flips open with a snap, revealing a docking ring
WIDE, gentle drift: the station sweeps over the curved planet, the tiny capsule trailing just behind it
CLOSE-UP, low angle: the docking ring meets the station port and locks with a heavy clunk
OVERHEAD, static: the joined capsule and station glide together above swirling clouds

blocks.vo_line: On October first, NASA's Crew Thirteen made it in seven hours fifty-five minutes, the fastest station trip by any American spacecraft.
blocks.through_line_state: the capsule sits on top of the slim rocket and rides it up
shots: WIDE, static: the slim white rocket stands on the seaside pad with the capsule on top, steam rolling out
CLOSE-UP, low angle: the engines ignite in a bright orange burst and the pad shakes
MEDIUM, crane up: the rocket climbs past the tower on a thick column of flame
EXTREME CLOSE-UP, static: the capsule pops free from the rocket's tip with a spring-like snap
HIGH ANGLE WIDE, slow push-in: the capsule arcs over the horizon as the sky darkens into space

blocks.vo_line: Distance was never the problem. The station circles Earth about every ninety minutes, moving at roughly seventeen thousand five hundred miles an hour.
blocks.through_line_state: the capsule watches the station streak past along the planet's edge
shots: CLOSE-UP, gentle drift: the station's solar wings tilt and catch a flash of sunlight
WIDE, static: the station streaks along the glowing edge of the planet, leaving a soft trail
EXTREME CLOSE-UP, push-in: the planet's surface rushes by beneath a solar wing
MEDIUM, orbit: the capsule hangs behind as the station pulls away with a whoosh
HIGH ANGLE WIDE, static: the station completes a full loop of the planet and snaps back into view

blocks.vo_line: A rocket cannot simply climb straight up. It must first match that enormous sideways velocity, then gradually chase the station around the planet.
blocks.through_line_state: the capsule falls back when thrown straight up, then curves into orbit and gives chase
shots: WIDE, static: the whole planet turns slowly while the slim rocket shoots straight up from it like a dart
CLOSE-UP, low angle: the capsule stalls at the top of its climb and drops back with a bounce
MEDIUM, gentle drift: a second rocket leans over and curves sideways around the planet
EXTREME CLOSE-UP, static: the capsule's thrusters fire and it slides onto a glowing ring-shaped track
OVERHEAD, slow push-in: the capsule chases the station around the ring, the gap shrinking

blocks.vo_line: And there's essentially one opportunity a day, the brief moment Earth's rotation carries the launch pad directly underneath the station's orbital path.
blocks.through_line_state: the capsule waits on the rocket as the station's track slides overhead
shots: LOW ANGLE MEDIUM, static: the rocket and capsule wait on the pad as the tiny station sweeps a glowing track across the sky above
EXTREME CLOSE-UP, push-in: a round dial on the tower clicks around to a single lit mark
HIGH ANGLE WIDE, gentle drift: the coastline rotates until the pad slides directly under the glowing track
CLOSE-UP, static: the track and the pad line up and a green light snaps on
MEDIUM, crane up: the engines light and the rocket leaps off the pad

blocks.vo_line: The rocket wasn't any faster. SpaceX said the station was in an opportune spot, the shortest chase the company has ever flown.
blocks.through_line_state: the capsule reaches orbit with the station already just ahead
shots: MEDIUM, low angle: the capsule pops off the rocket's upper stage over the planet's glowing edge and the station is already right ahead
EXTREME CLOSE-UP, static: the capsule's nose cone swings open with a click
WIDE, gentle drift: only a short gap separates capsule and station along the curve of the planet
CLOSE-UP, slow push-in: the capsule's thrusters puff once and it glides forward
OVERHEAD, static: the capsule slots onto the station port with a stamp-like clunk

blocks.vo_line: Still, the all-time crew record belongs to a Russian Soyuz: three hours, three minutes, in twenty twenty. Which is wild, because
blocks.through_line_state: the capsule laps the planet twice and docks, then returns to closing in from below
shots: CLOSE-UP, gentle drift: the capsule whips around the planet once, leaving a bright looping trail
HIGH ANGLE WIDE, static: a second loop of trail wraps the planet and ends at the station
EXTREME CLOSE-UP, push-in: the docking ring locks shut with a sharp clunk
MEDIUM, orbit: the station turns slowly with the capsule attached, solar wings glinting
LOW ANGLE WIDE, static: the capsule floats just below the station above the curved planet, settling into the opening view
